title: Palace, office or citadel?
hook: Did the palace, offices and citadel change together?

knows: Selected accounts can describe distinct institutions and dated changes.
doesNotKnow: Fatimid, Seljuk and Ayyubid institutions and the timing of separate changes

objective: Fatimid, Seljuk and Ayyubid institutions and the timing of separate changes

claims.text: TDV distinguishes Fatimid Cairo’s restricted palace and later citadel plan from Damascus’s atabeg government and Saladin’s military headquarters. The 1171 Cairo and 1174 Damascus changes supply different institutions and scopes. A plan is not completed construction; shared dynastic affiliation does not establish uniform administration, identical palace access or universal assent.

recall.question: Which evidence prevents a single uniform institutional transition?
options: The records describe different palace, government and military institutions.
A shared dynasty made every institution change at once.
recall.why: Cairo’s restricted caliphal palace and planned citadel differ from Tughtegin’s government and Damascus’s later military headquarters.

care: Keep named local governing relations and separately dated changes, not blanket Fatimid/Seljuk/Ayyubid labels.
